newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says Netanyahu "nose" comment unfortunate.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says Netanyahu "nose" comment unfortunate.

text.p: Egypt described on Tuesday Israeli criticism of its Middle East policy as unfortunate and advised Israel Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to watch out for his own nose rather than making remarks about Egypt's.

Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa was responding to Netanyahu who said on Sunday that in threatening to postpone a Middle East economic conference Egypt was acting "like a man who cuts off his nose to spite his face".
"It was unfortunate talk," he told reporters. "He'd do best to keep off Egypt's nose so that Egypt keeps off his nose."
On a more serious note, Moussa said that the economic conference, scheduled to take place in Egypt in November, was not the only element in steps towards Middle East peace.

Egypt has said that unless there is progress towards peace, it might postpone the conference, which would try to integrate Israel into the regional economy. It blames Israel for the current stalemate in talks with Syria and the Palestinians.

Moussa said: "The important thing is to move forward on all peace tracks and that Israel respects its signatures and its commitments because not respecting the commitments will lead to a crisis threatening peace. Israel will be responsible."
But he added: "The conference is still on and there are seven weeks left. We hope they will be used and exploited in favour of supporting the peace process, not destroying it."
Egypt's main government newspaper questioned Netanyahu's sanity on Tuesday and described his remarks on Egyptian policy as impudent and foolish.

The newspaper al-Ahram, in its regular leader, said: "What is this arrogance and impudence which has afflicted Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu? The day before yesterday he made statements which lack completely the decorum and good manners necessary in the discourse between states."

"This man, unaware of the realities of life, seems to have forgotten the leading and pioneering role of Egypt in making peace in the Middle East...He seems to be unaware that without Egypt Israel would not have a foothold in any Arab country.
"This is shameful for a man who knows no shame and he must think the matter over from start to finish," it added.
The newspaper said people may have excused Netanyahu's statements during the Israeli election campaign earler this year but now that he was in power there was no excuse.

"These latest statements are even more foolish and stupid than his statements during the campaign... If such statements are made by someone in a position of responsibility, it calls for an investigation into his powers of reason," it added.
